::: {#exr-binary-trace}
#### Tracing a recursive Racket function

The Racket function `binary` takes a non-negative integer (@def-nonnegative-integers) `n`
and returns a string:

```racket
(define (binary n)
  (if (< n 2)
      (number->string n)
      (string-append (binary (quotient n 2))
                     (number->string (remainder n 2)))))
```

Here

- `(if test a b)` returns `a` when `test` is true and `b` when it is false;
- `(quotient n 2)` is $\floor{n / 2}$, the floor (@def-floor) of $n / 2$;
- `(remainder n 2)` is the remainder, 0 or 1, left after dividing `n` by 2;
- `number->string` turns a number into the string of its digits;
- `string-append` joins two strings into one.

Run `(binary 6)` by hand:
write down each call of `binary` that it makes, and the string that each call returns.

:::
